reasons: Fixed fallback user id can write to a shared cloud account.
Field mappings cover only three tables.
Only 7 of 28 sections were reviewed here.

terms.meaning: A named function a screen calls to change the data, such as adding a task.
A translation that renames app fields to match the cloud database columns.
Two naming styles. The app uses one and the database the other, so names must be translated.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports
sections.what: Loads the data types, starter data, helper functions, sound, local database and cloud connection.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Starter data is loaded from another file, so a fresh install may show example entries.

sections.name: mapToSupabasePayload
sections.title: Cloud field mapping
sections.what: Converts internship, hackathon and task records into the column names the cloud expects. Other tables pass through unchanged.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app and the cloud database use different naming styles.
sections.watch_out: Tables without a mapping send raw field names, so a mismatch will make the save fail.

sections.name: syncToSupabase
sections.title: Cloud save and delete
sections.what: Sends one change to the cloud for the signed-in user, or for a built-in fallback user if no one is signed in. If the call fails, the change is queued for later.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the cloud in step with the app, even offline.
sections.watch_out: The fixed fallback user id means changes made without sign-in may be stored in one shared account.

sections.name: TabType
sections.title: Screen names
sections.what: Lists the names of every screen the user can open.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the compiler catch misspelled screen names.
sections.watch_out: A new screen must be added here as well as in the page.

sections.name: MomentumState (part 1)
sections.title: Shared state layout
sections.what: Describes everything the store holds: which screen and popups are open, every data list, and the background sound settings.
sections.why: Likely reason: one reference for what data exists.
sections.watch_out: Data list names must match the local database table names, or saving breaks.

sections.name: MomentumState (part 2)
sections.title: Focus timer and task actions
sections.what: Describes the focus timer state and actions, and the actions to add, change, delete and bulk-change tasks and their subtasks.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: The timer only counts while the one-second ticker in the page is running.

sections.name: MomentumState (part 3)
sections.title: Habits, routines, notes, calendar and courses
sections.what: Describes the actions for habits, routines, notes, calendar events, courses and assignments that screens call to change data.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 1)
sections.title: Store setup and cloud fetch
sections.what: Creates the app's central data store and begins pulling hackathons and internships from the online database. Rows that come back replace the list the app is showing for that type.
sections.why: Likely reason: the app keeps a local copy so it can work offline, then refreshes that copy from the cloud when it can.
sections.watch_out: Fetched rows replace the local list entirely, and the returned error is never checked, so a failed fetch looks the same as an empty result and items never uploaded can disappear.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 2)
sections.title: Fetching tasks and restoring local data
sections.what: Pulls tasks from the cloud the same way, then loads every saved list from the local Dexie database into the app. A local list that is empty keeps whatever the app already holds in memory.
sections.why: Likely reason: local storage restores the last session quickly, and the cloud copy is then merged in when it arrives.
sections.watch_out: Because an empty local list falls back to the in-memory value, a user who deletes everything may see the app's sample data return after a reload.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 3)
sections.title: Startup fallbacks and sample data
sections.what: After loading local data, asks the cloud for fresh data, including when local loading failed. It also starts the store with the app's sample data for every list and marks the mission control page as the first page shown.
sections.why: Likely reason: sample data lets a new user see a populated app before adding anything, and the cloud refresh runs as a backup path.
sections.watch_out: Sample data stays in place on a new device whenever the local database has no rows for that list.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 4)
sections.title: Ambient sound and focus timer state
sections.what: Lets the user start one background sound at a time and adjust its volume. It also holds the focus timer and its pause, reset and mode controls, with a default length for each mode.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeping timer and sound state in one store means every screen shows the same status.
sections.watch_out: The reset and mode code gives long breaks and the flow mode the 30-minute default, which may not be the intended length for those modes.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 5)
sections.title: Focus countdown tick and new tasks
sections.what: The countdown is meant to be called repeatedly, reducing the timer by one second each time. When it reaches zero, it plays a bell, shows confetti, saves a finished focus session, and awards XP and momentum. The start of adding a task also appears here.
sections.why: Likely reason: a timer kept in shared state keeps counting when the user changes screens.
sections.watch_out: The reward uses the mode's fixed length (50 or 10 minutes) rather than the length actually started, so a custom timer is rewarded incorrectly.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 6)
sections.title: Saving task changes and completing tasks
sections.what: Adds a new task to the list, sends it to the cloud, and adds a calendar entry when it has a due date. Updating a task changes only the matching one, and toggling status marks it complete or back to to-do with a sound and confetti.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the calendar link, though it keeps due dates visible on the calendar automatically.
sections.watch_out: Completing a task awards XP, but reopening it takes nothing back, so repeatedly completing and reopening a task can earn XP again each time.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 7)
sections.title: Bulk edits, deletion and subtasks
sections.what: Applies one action such as complete, change status, change priority, or delete to many tasks at once. Deleting a task also removes its calendar entry, and subtasks can be added and ticked off inside a task.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the separate bulk action, though it lets users change many tasks in one step.
sections.watch_out: Adding or ticking a subtask does not send the change to the cloud, so the subtask state may differ on another device.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 8)
sections.title: Habit creation, editing and archiving
sections.what: Adds, edits, deletes, pauses and archives habits. Pause and archive act as toggles, so pressing them again returns the habit to active.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the separate pause and archive actions, though they let a habit stay in the list without counting toward daily work.
sections.watch_out: None of these habit actions in this section send changes to the cloud or the local database, so habit changes may be lost on reload unless saved elsewhere.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 9)
sections.title: Duplicating and logging habit progress
sections.what: Copies a habit with a Copy label and resets its streaks. Marks a day as skipped, restores a habit to active, and starts logging completions, with more confetti at streak milestones.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the duplicate action, though it lets users reuse a habit setup.
sections.watch_out: Streaks only go up here: missed days do not reset them, and logging the same day twice adds to the streak again.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 10)
sections.title: Habit stats and routine checklists
sections.what: Saves the new habit streak and success rate and awards 60 XP for logging a habit. A routine is a checklist, and when every item is ticked it is marked done for the day with an XP reward. The reset action clears every routine checkmark.
sections.why: Likely reason: rewards for finishing a routine encourage daily use, and the reset supports a new day.
sections.watch_out: Unticking an item and ticking it again re-awards the routine XP each time the list becomes complete.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 11)
sections.title: Notes and calendar events
sections.what: Adds a note at the top of the list with a created time, edits it with a new updated time, and deletes it. Also adds and removes calendar entries.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Notes and manually added calendar entries are not sent to the cloud or saved to the local database in this section.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 12)
sections.title: Course list and GPA goal
sections.what: Adds, edits and deletes courses, and saves a target GPA on the user's profile. Changes to courses are saved to the local database.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code.
sections.watch_out: Courses and the GPA goal are saved only locally, so they will not appear on another device.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 13)
sections.title: Assignments with calendar entries and alerts
sections.what: Adding an assignment also creates a deadline calendar entry and a notification. Deleting an assignment removes its calendar entry too.
sections.why: Likely reason: deadlines show up on the calendar and in alerts without the user having to add them twice.
sections.watch_out: Changing an assignment's due date does not move its calendar entry, so the calendar can show the old date.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 14)
sections.title: Internship add and deadline calendar
sections.what: Adds an internship, saves it to the cloud and local database, and creates a deadline calendar entry when a deadline is set. Editing keeps that calendar entry in step with the internship, and creates one if it is missing.
sections.why: Likely reason: internship deadlines are kept on the calendar so they are not missed.
sections.watch_out: Clearing an internship's deadline leaves its old calendar entry in place, since updates only change the calendar when a deadline exists.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 15)
sections.title: Deleting internships and adding hackathons
sections.what: Deleting an internship removes it from the cloud, the local database and the calendar. Adding a hackathon picks a calendar date from its submission deadline, registration deadline or start date, then saves it. Editing updates the matching calendar entry.
sections.why: Likely reason: the fallback order lets a hackathon get a calendar date even when only some dates are entered.
sections.watch_out: Adding a hackathon never sets an end date, while the cloud table requires one, so the cloud save may be rejected unless the entry form supplies it.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 16)
sections.title: Competitions, papers and certificates
sections.what: Deleting a hackathon removes it from the cloud and local database and removes its calendar entry. Competitions get a calendar entry at a fixed time, and papers and certificates can be added and removed.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the fixed competition time.
sections.watch_out: Competitions, research papers and certifications are not saved to the cloud or the local database in this section, so they may be lost on reload.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 17)
sections.title: Goals, projects and alerts
sections.what: Adds, edits and deletes goals. Ticking a milestone updates the goal's percent complete, with confetti when it reaches 100. Adds and deletes projects, marks alerts as read, clears alerts, and updates settings.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for the milestone percent, though it shows progress toward each goal at a glance.
sections.watch_out: Goal, project, alert and settings changes are not saved to the cloud or the local database in this section.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 18)
sections.title: XP, levels and momentum score
sections.what: Adds XP and coins, and raises the level once when the XP passes the threshold. Recalculates the momentum score from tasks, habits, routines and focus time, and keeps the last seven days' average and the best score.
sections.why: Likely reason: a single momentum number gives the user one progress measure across all parts of the app.
sections.watch_out: The app raises the next level threshold by 1500, while the database starts it at 1000, and the reason for the difference is not stated in the code.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 19)
sections.title: Daily streak and freeze tokens
sections.what: On a new day, compares the last active date with today. A one-day gap keeps the streak, a single missed day uses a freeze token if one is left or resets the streak, and longer gaps reset it. Export downloads a full backup of the store as a JSON file.
sections.why: Likely reason: freeze tokens reward regular use while forgiving a single missed day.
sections.watch_out: Dates are converted into times, which can shift the day count for users far from UTC, and this behavior is not checked in the code.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 20)
sections.title: CSV export and JSON import
sections.what: Downloads five spreadsheet files for tasks, habits, goals, assignments and internships. Import replaces the app's data with a backup if the file has the expected pieces, and returns true or false. Reset clears most lists while keeping the user's name and role.
sections.why: Likely reason: spreadsheet files are for users who want to review data outside the app, and import supports restoring a backup.
sections.watch_out: The reset action is named as going to demo data, but it empties the lists and does not restore the sample data.

sections.name: useMomentumStore (part 21)
sections.title: Profile, persona and clear-all
sections.what: Sets the user's name and role when a name is given, and saves the chosen persona to the local database. Clear-all empties most lists and resets the momentum score, XP and streak.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code for keeping level and coins when clearing data.
sections.watch_out: Clear-all changes only the in-memory data and does not delete the local database copy or the cloud rows, so the data may return on reload.

summary: The central data store that holds all of the app's information, such as tasks, habits, notes and goals, and saves changes locally and to the cloud.
purpose: Gives every screen one shared source of truth and keeps the data safe between visits.
why: Likely reason: one store avoids each screen keeping its own copy of the data.
how: 1) Defines the field names used for cloud tables. 2) Defines what the store holds and the actions it offers. 3) Saves each change to the local database and then to the cloud, queuing it if the cloud call fails.
inputs: Actions called from screens, the signed-in user, and the local and cloud databases.
outputs: Updated data for all screens, saved local copies, and cloud records.
risks: When no one is signed in, cloud changes go to a fixed built-in user id. Only three tables have field mappings, so other records send raw field names that may not match the cloud columns.
debug: If data does not save, check the browser console for Supabase sync error lines and the sync queue in IndexedDB. If changes appear in the wrong account, check the fixed fallback user id.
